text:
maya: Heads-up — we're seeing missing child spans for ~2.7% of traces that cross the kafka-exporter path since the collector bump to 0.46.3 last night. Alert 02:41 UTC. Root spans present, but many children never show up in the trace UI.
tracebot: Alert: trace_span_loss_rate > 2% (kafka-exporter -> consumer) — rule: otel.pipeline.span.loss.rate. Details: k:prod, cluster:eu-west1.
kevin: Is this all models or a subset of services?
luca: quick check: looks concentrated on requests that hit the router -> transformation service -> indexing. Not global.
maya: suspecting exporter side. We rolled a config tweak to kafka-exporter batching + key template yesterday (DEV-3872).
devon: +1 — I rolled that patch (change to message.key template) in the collector chart at 23:58 UTC. Link: https://git.internal/redwood/collector/commit/abc123
kevin: can we dump a sample Kafka message and inspect key vs headers? run kafka-console-consumer on partition.
sre-oncall: grabbing a sample now. command: kafka-console-consumer --bootstrap-server kafka.prod:9092 --topic otel-spans-v1 --partition 4 --offset 120345 --max-messages 50 --property print.key=true
luca: FYI here's an example of the consumer output I pulled (trimmed):
```
key: 9a1b2c3d4e5f6a7b
headers: traceparent=00-4a3b2c...-01, tracestate=rw=1
value: {"span_id":"b3c4d5e6","parent_span_id":"a1b2c3d4"...}
```
kevin: that key looks like 16 hex chars only. trace_id should be 32 hex chars.
devon: yeah — the exporter template was set to `message_key: "%{trace_id:16}"` because we thought we only needed a short key for partitioning. That was deliberate in the patch (my bad).
maya: wait, the collector downstream consumer uses the message key to assemble traces (we added that optimization in Q4). If the key is only half the trace_id, consumer reconstruct can mis-associate children.
kevin: that lines up — partial keys mean multiple different full trace_ids map to the same key namespace or vice versa and our join logic fails, so children can be overlooked when the consumer expects key==full_trace_id.
luca: to confirm — I grepped for headers with full traceparent and found many messages where headers HAVE full traceparent but key != trace_id. Example: header traceparent=00-4a3b2c1d9e8f... but key=1d9e8f... (last 16 chars).
sre-oncall: quick mitigation: set exporter to not use message key so consumers fall back to header-based grouping. I'm going to patch the config to remove message_key template and roll to 1 node first.
ops-bot: deploy-batch started for chart collector/exporter to staging replicas 1 -> 0. Rollout id: deploy-2026-03-20-02:58
kevin: also we should update consumer logic to avoid relying solely on the kafka key. Fallback to traceparent header when key length != 32 hex. I'll open a PR to add validation + a metric.
devon: PR: https://git.internal/redwood/otel-consumer/pull/492 — adds header fallbacks and a kmsg_key_length gauge.
maya: timeline: revert exporter key template now (mitigation) and then patch consumer (longer-term). Any objections?
luca: +1 — also add a health check that alerts when key_len != 32 for >0.5% of messages per minute.
kevin: noting for postmortem: config change (message_key: "%{trace_id:16}") introduced at 2026-03-19 23:58 UTC; symptom: children missing in UI; scope: services that rely on consumer-join-by-key optimization. Root cause: truncation of trace_id used as kafka message key.
sre-oncall: rolled config out to 3 collector pods (canary) at 02:59 UTC. initial error rate improved in 5m window.
maya: thanks. Can someone grab a short postmortem and put in /postmortems? We should include suggested follow-ups: revert unsafe shortcuts, consumer header fallback, key validation metric, and a small doc explaining when it's ok to use kafka key vs header.
kevin: I'll take the postmortem. Putting checklist in PR.
tracebot: System: Incident closed (mitigation: exporter key removed). Follow-up: postmortem requested by maya.
maya: nice work everyone. :thumbsup:
